newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS says new UK flights aimed at BA.
newsitem.headline: SAS says new UK flights aimed at BA.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System said on Tuesday that its increased flights to London with partner British Midland were aimed at fighting heightened competition from British Airways.

"We are doing it to get a stronger position in competition with British Airways and -- in a co-ordinated programme with British Midland -- to offer a better schedule to our customers," SAS Senior Vice-President Vagn Soerensen told Reuters.
SAS -- which owns 40 percent of British Midland -- said earlier that from April 21 the partners would open three new connections between London and Scandinavia.
It said that British Midland would fly a daily round trip with a Boeing 737 from Copenhagen, Oslo and Gothenburg to London's Heathrow.
"The new connections are a widening of the existing code share cooperation between SAS and British Midland," SAS said.
British Midland already flies between London and Bergen, Norway as well as between Glasgow and Edinburgh and Copenhagen in cooperation with SAS.

British Airways has been building a network of Nordic allies and increasing its activities on SAS' home turf. Denmark's Maersk Air has close ties to BA which also has a franchise agreement with Sun Air of Denmark.
BA's frequent flier programme is linked to Norway's Braathens SAFE and its chief executive, Bob Ayling, said on Tuesday he would not rule out more BA moves in Nordic skies.
"I wouldn't like to say that's the end of developments in that area, but I am not announcing any changes today," Ayling told a news conference in Stockholm.
"We compete head-to-head now with SAS here. We have very strong expansion plans both for domestic and international flights," Ayling said.
"We see the Scandinavian market, and in particular the Swedish market, as being a natural market for a company which is based in northern Europe."
